Because this task relies on blind luck (i.e. natural genetic mutation), AI may come handy in enhancing our chances of succeeding. Prior to using AI, I'd guess the probabilities similar to Soloveichik's 2022 statistical analysis on 2600 foods, guessing that the bounded average probability of success is 0.08. However, developments in AI, as enumerated by Razfahbazi in 2024, indicated a new possibility that merging human and AI intelligence systems could boost productivity. Thus, going by Soloveichik's prediction, there is a 0.08 probability that a dairy cow with the desired characteristics should be found, and a 0.1 probability that the same result would be found with the aid of AI technologies; both probabilities and their lower bounds are still decreasing with time. Game theory literature could come handy here to find the optimal probabilities with the summation of all probabilities to a bound and the minimum raising of probabilities to make certain combinations of outcomes occur within a specified time frame.
